- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

[metadata]
task_id = "carbon-design-system__carbon-21854-mm"
title = "[Bug]: cds-tabs with selection-mode=\"manual\" dispatches cds-tabs-selected event on keyboard navigation, but tab is not selected"
repository_name = "carbon-design-system/carbon"
repo_url = "https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon"
issue_number = 21854
pr_number = 22018
base_commit = "1a9ccca45f0671c874a9cf83d244ab81f7adc7ab"
fix_commit = "9595886294b39b526bbb5bf158824e0dcafce0e1"
task_type = "temporal_interaction"
language = "TypeScript"
framework = "Web Components (Lit)"
cross_file = true
visual_essentiality = "required"
difficulty = "hard"
difficulty_explanation = """
The prose states only the interaction contract that must hold. Everything needed to act on
it lives in the attached GIF: which of the repository's ~100 components is involved, which
of its two framework implementations is running, which selection mode it is in, which
custom event is at fault, and what that event's payload looks like. The recording shows
focus moving to a neighbouring tab while the previously selected tab stays selected and its
panel stays open, with the console logging a selection event and its detail object. Without
the recording the description matches the React tabs, the web-components tabs and the
content switcher equally well, so the visual sequence is what makes the task actionable.

The starting state carries several independent defects along the same interaction path, and
they mask each other: keyboard movement emits the selection event that should only follow
explicit activation, while explicit activation changes the selection without emitting it;
the manual-mode keyboard cursor is not the state that movement advances, so movement past
the first step, and activation afterwards, act on the wrong tab; movement stops at both ends
of the list instead of continuing onto the opposite one; movement does not skip tabs that
cannot be selected; the jump-to-either-end keys select outright instead of moving focus; the
pointer does not hand its position over to the keyboard; and the selected state exposed to
assistive technology tracks the focus rather than the selection. The defects are spread
across the tabs element, the tab element and the content switcher base class the tabs extend,
so a fix confined to the file named by the symptom cannot pass. The task names no file, no
method, no key, no event, no attribute and no expected code change.

The verifier checks observable behavior only. It drives real key presses and clicks in a
headless browser and asserts what a user or assistive technology can perceive: where the
focus is, which tab is selected, the component value, the accessible selected state, and the
selection events with their payloads. Existing content-switcher click, keyboard-selection,
selectedIndex and manual-mode behavior must keep passing. No test refers to internal method
names, interaction-type values, event-gating logic or source structure, so any implementation
that produces the specified behavior scores full marks.
"""
files_edited = [
  "packages/web-components/src/components/content-switcher/content-switcher.ts",
  "packages/web-components/src/components/tabs/tabs.ts",
  "packages/web-components/src/components/tabs/tab.ts",
]
f2p = [
  "cds-tabs manual selection mode > should move focus without changing selection or emitting cds-tabs-selected during arrow-key navigation",
  "cds-tabs manual selection mode > should emit cds-tabs-selected when the focused tab is explicitly selected with the keyboard",
  "cds-tabs manual selection mode > should wrap around both ends of the tab list during arrow-key navigation",
  "cds-tabs manual selection mode > should skip disabled tabs when moving focus and when selecting",
  "cds-tabs manual selection mode > should move focus to the first and last tab without changing the selection",
  "cds-tabs manual selection mode > should expose the selected state on the selected tab rather than on the focused one",
  "cds-tabs manual selection mode > should continue keyboard navigation from the tab most recently selected with the pointer",
]
p2p = [
  "cds-content-switcher > should apply selectedIndex correctly",
  "cds-content-switcher > should emit event on click with matching details",
  "cds-content-switcher > should emit event on keydown (ArrowRight/ArrowLeft)",
  "cds-content-switcher > should emit an event on click when selectionMode is manual",
  "cds-content-switcher > should emit an event on Enter or Space when selectionMode is manual",
]

content.content:
# Unexpected interaction behavior

The recording below shows a keyboard interaction with a component of this repository, in the selection mode the recording puts it in, and the outcome that interaction produces. That outcome is wrong.

Reproduce the interaction, then make the component behave like this in that mode:

- Moving through the items with the keyboard only moves the focus: the current selection stays where it is and no selection event is emitted. This holds for every step, including the moves that jump straight to either end of the list.
- Moving through the items always lands on an item that can be selected, and running off either end of the list continues onto the opposite end.
- Moving on from an item that was just selected with the pointer continues from that item.
- Explicitly activating the focused item with the keyboard selects it and emits the selection event, carrying the payload the recording shows for that event.
- The selected state exposed to assistive technology follows the selection, never the focus.

Behavior that is already correct, both in this component and in anything it shares code with, must keep working.

![Issue](/app/.harbor_assets/bug.gif)

FROM node:24-bookworm

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
      git ca-certificates \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

ENV CI=true

WORKDIR /app

# [IMPORTANT] Bug patches live outside environment/assets/ (build-only input, never
# agent-visible evidence) and are staged in a TEMP path so they can be baked into the
# base snapshot without ever reaching /app.
COPY bugs/ /tmp/bugs/

# Clone, pin to the base commit, then STRIP .git so the agent cannot inspect the fix PR
# or future history (anti-cheat).
#
# [IMPORTANT] Every bug patch is applied BEFORE the snapshot below, so the defects are
# part of harbor_base -- the exact state the agent starts from. A patch that fails to
# apply fails the build instead of silently producing a task with no bug in it.
#
# [IMPORTANT] harbor_base = base commit + all bug patches, re-inited as a single commit
# so the verifier can reset test files; git apply still works without upstream history.
RUN git init -q \
 && git remote add origin https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon \
 && git fetch --depth 1 origin 1a9ccca45f0671c874a9cf83d244ab81f7adc7ab \
 && git checkout 1a9ccca45f0671c874a9cf83d244ab81f7adc7ab \
 && rm -rf .git \
 && for p in /tmp/bugs/*.patch; do git apply "$p" || exit 1; done \
 && rm -rf /tmp/bugs \
 && git init -q \
 && git -c user.email=h@l -c user.name=h add -A \
 && git -c user.email=h@l -c user.name=h commit -q -m base \
 && git tag harbor_base

RUN corepack enable && yarn install --immutable

# Bake the FULL build (web-components + its workspace deps) at base-commit state. Verify
# time only needs to rebuild @carbon/web-components itself (fast) since the fix/test
# patches never touch other workspace packages.
RUN yarn lerna run build --scope='@carbon/web-components' --include-dependencies

RUN mkdir -p /logs /app/.harbor_assets
COPY assets/ /app/.harbor_assets/

CMD ["bash"]

set -euxo pipefail
cd /app

apply_if_nonempty() {
  local p="$1"
  if [ -f "$p" ] && grep -q '[^[:space:]]' "$p"; then
    git apply "$p" 2>/dev/null || patch -p1 < "$p"
  fi
}

apply_if_nonempty /solution/fix.patch
echo "Applied fix.patch."

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Verifier for carbon-design-system__carbon-21854-mm (cds-tabs / cds-content-switcher manual
selection-mode event contract).

Reads the per-test JSON report produced by test.sh (a custom @web/test-runner reporter dumps
the REAL Mocha pass/fail/missing status for every test in the two harness test files) and
computes a scalar reward. Reward is BINARY: 1.0 only when every f2p passes AND every p2p
still passes; a strict subset of f2p passing or any p2p regression is 0.0, not partial
credit -- the four count keys in reward.json already carry how close it got. NEVER inspects
source for the fix -- reward derives solely from the test report.
"""
import atexit
import json
import os
import sys

CONF = json.load(open('/tests/config.json'))
F2P = CONF['f2p']
P2P = CONF['p2p']
REPORT = '/logs/verifier/results.json'   # keep in sync with test.sh's reporter output path
REWARD = '/logs/verifier/reward.txt'
CANON_JSON = '/logs/verifier/reward.json'
_canon = {}


def canon_reward(f2p_passed, f2p_total, p2p_passed, p2p_total, rubric):
    """THE reward policy for the whole corpus. BINARY -- there is no partial credit."""
    f, t = int(f2p_passed), int(f2p_total)
    p, q = int(p2p_passed), int(p2p_total)
    solved = bool(t) and f == t and p == q
    tests_passed = 1.0 if solved else 0.0
    _canon.clear()
    _canon.update({
        'reward': 0.0 if rubric == 'fail' else tests_passed,
        'tests_passed': tests_passed,
        'f2p_passed': f, 'f2p_total': t,
        'p2p_passed': p, 'p2p_total': q,
        'rubric_passed': {'pass': 1, 'fail': 0}.get(rubric, -1),
    })
    return _canon['reward']


@atexit.register
def _canon_flush():
    if not _canon:
        return
    try:
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(CANON_JSON), exist_ok=True)
        with open(CANON_JSON, 'w') as h:
            json.dump(_canon, h, indent=2)
        with open(REWARD, 'w') as h:
            h.write(str(_canon['reward']))
    except OSError as exc:
        print(f'WARNING: could not write {CANON_JSON}: {exc}', file=sys.stderr)


def rubric_verdict(argv):
    """The verdict test.sh hands in as `--rubric pass|fail|""`. Anything else means "not
    graded", which must never penalise the run."""
    if '--rubric' not in argv:
        return None
    i = argv.index('--rubric')
    value = argv[i + 1].strip().lower() if i + 1 < len(argv) else ''
    return value if value in ('pass', 'fail') else None


def load_results() -> dict:
    """Return {full_test_title: 'pass'|'fail'|'skip'} from test.sh's JSON report."""
    if not os.path.exists(REPORT):
        return {}
    try:
        data = json.load(open(REPORT))
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as e:
        print(f'[verifier] report parse error: {e}', file=sys.stderr)
        return {}
    return data if isinstance(data, dict) else {}


def matched(idents: list, results: dict) -> dict:
    out = {}
    for ident in idents:
        # config.json identifiers are the plain "<describe> > <it>" full mocha title; the
        # reporter in test.sh keys results the same way, so this is an exact lookup, never
        # a substring scan.
        out[ident] = results.get(ident, 'missing')
    return out


def main() -> int:
    r = load_results()
    f2p = matched(F2P, r)
    p2p = matched(P2P, r)

    f2p_pass = [k for k, v in f2p.items() if v == 'pass']
    p2p_pass = [k for k, v in p2p.items() if v == 'pass']

    reward = canon_reward(len(f2p_pass), len(F2P), len(p2p_pass), len(P2P),
                          rubric_verdict(sys.argv[1:]))

    print(json.dumps({
        'reward': reward,
        'f2p': f2p,
        'p2p': p2p,
        'f2p_pass_count': len(f2p_pass),
        'p2p_pass_count': len(p2p_pass),
        'testcases_total': len(F2P) + len(P2P),
        'testcases_seen': sum(1 for v in {**f2p, **p2p}.values() if v != 'missing'),
    }))
    return 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())
